exclude-rules._comment: G115 (integer conversion): the flagged int/uint64 to uint32/int32 conversions are protobuf field widths and metric counters (ports, counts, seconds, byte sizes) bounded well below 2^31 by their sources. A blanket exclusion is used because gosec cannot see the bounds.

G304 (file inclusion via variable): every flagged path comes from operator configuration, the data/state directory or a CLI flag, never directly from a network request. Paths that do originate from the API are validated against allowlists before use (priv verbs, backup restore names, update staging).

G204 (subprocess with variable): commands are launched without a shell (argv form). Arguments that originate from jobs are validated against allowlists in the priv verbs; the remaining binaries are fixed OS paths (icacls, smartctl, systemctl).

G302/G306 (permissions above 0600): only public material (CA and leaf certificates, public keys, signatures, SAN lists), executables that must be 0755/0700, and config read by the agent group (0640) use these modes. Private keys are written 0600 and are not flagged.

G402 (InsecureSkipVerify): intentional. probe.go inspects certificates of arbitrary monitored hosts (expiry checks); notify.go honours a per-channel opt-in skip_verify setting; selfupdate/apply.go and the server healthcheck only talk to this server's own loopback listener, which may use a self-signed certificate.
G123 (VerifyPeerCertificate with resumption): the agent TLS config sets no ClientSessionCache, so sessions are never resumed and the CA-pin verifier runs on every handshake.
G404 (math/rand): used only for reconnect backoff jitter, which is not security sensitive.
G124 (cookie attributes): HttpOnly and SameSite are set; Secure is deliberately derived from the request (isHTTPS) so plain-HTTP installs can still sign in.
G702/G703 (taint analysis): sentrel-sign is an operator CLI that signs a file the operator names; acl_windows.go runs icacls.exe (no shell) on a path the agent itself derived.

G110 (decompression bomb): backup restore copies tar entries from an archive uploaded by an authenticated admin. Real but low risk; recommended fix is wrapping the entry in io.LimitReader. Scoped to this one file so the rule still guards the rest of the tree.
